nodes.title: Barrelled spaces and nonarchimedean Banach–Steinhaus
nodes.statement: A locally convex K-space V is barrelled when every closed O_K-lattice is open. Fréchet spaces are barrelled; locally convex inductive limits of barrelled spaces are barrelled, hence Hausdorff LB-spaces are barrelled. For barrelled V and a locally convex W, a pointwise bounded family of continuous linear maps V → W is equicontinuous. Over spherically complete K, a Hausdorff bornological or barrelled V has a topological embedding V → (V′_b)′_b; in particular the bidual map is continuous. This does not assert that the map is surjective or that bornological and barrelled are the same property.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·|, with ring of integers O_K = {a : |a| ≤ 1} and a fixed π ∈ K with 0 < |π| < 1; a lattice in a K-vector space V is an O_K-submodule L with K·L = V.
K is spherically complete for polar and bidual statements; barrelledness and Banach–Steinhaus do not need that additional assumption.
proofSteps: For each closed target lattice M, the intersection of inverse images under a pointwise bounded family is a closed lattice: pointwise boundedness makes it absorbing. Barrelledness makes it open, giving equicontinuity (Schneider 6.15).

In a complete metrizable space Baire applied to the countably many scalar dilates of a closed lattice gives interior, hence openness (Schneider 8.2). For a locally convex final topology, pull a closed lattice back to each barrelled stage and use the open-lattice final criterion.

For bidual continuity, any strongly bounded family in V′ is equicontinuous by Schneider 6.12 (bornological case) or 6.16 (barrelled case). Its polar is therefore an open neighbourhood. Hahn–Banach separation and Schneider Remark 9.8 give injectivity and the continuity of the inverse on the image (Lemma 9.9).

nodes.title: Pseudo-polars and the nonarchimedean bipolar theorem
nodes.statement: For an O_K-submodule A of a Hausdorff locally convex space V, define its pseudo-polar A^p = {ℓ∈V′ : |ℓ(a)|<1 for every a∈A}, and its pseudo-bipolar A^{pp} using the same strict inequality against A^p. Over spherically complete K, A^{pp} is the closure of A. Pseudo-polars reverse inclusion; for bounded A, A^p is an open lattice of V′_b; for an open lattice L of V, L^p is equicontinuous. These use strict inequalities; ordinary unit-ball polars may be compared by multiplication by the fixed π, and must not be substituted without that adjustment.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·|, with ring of integers O_K = {a : |a| ≤ 1} and a fixed π ∈ K with 0 < |π| < 1; a lattice in a K-vector space V is an O_K-submodule L with K·L = V.
K is spherically complete for polar and bidual statements; barrelledness and Banach–Steinhaus do not need that additional assumption.
proofSteps: The basic topology and inclusion properties follow by intersections of evaluation inverse images and the absorbing condition (Schneider Lemma 13.1).

Use the maximal orthogonal-family gauge construction of Schneider 13.2 to find a continuous form separating a point from a closed O_K-submodule with value 1 at the point and values of norm <1 on the submodule (13.3). Each coordinate form is obtained by Hahn–Banach. This strengthened separation, not just ordinary ≤1 separation, is what is needed.

The pseudo-bipolar is closed and contains A. The strengthened separation excludes every point outside closure(A), proving 13.4. The lattice gauge construction uses the finite-dimensional almost-orthogonal estimates already planned in banach-c0-models.

nodes.title: Strong operator spaces and Banach factorisation for LB-to-Fréchet maps
nodes.statement: Let V be a Hausdorff semi-complete LB-space and F a Fréchet space over spherically complete K. For a Banach-stage presentation V=lim→V_n, the restriction map L_b(V,F) → lim←L_b(V_n,F) is a topological isomorphism; this operator space is Fréchet. Every continuous linear f:V→F factors continuously through a Banach space (a BH-map); equivalently some open lattice in V has bounded image in F. The associated polar input is that a continuous map F′_b→G to a Fréchet G sends some zero neighbourhood to a bounded set. No assertion is made for arbitrary LF-spaces or for non-semi-complete LB-spaces.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·|, with ring of integers O_K = {a : |a| ≤ 1} and a fixed π ∈ K with 0 < |π| < 1; a lattice in a K-vector space V is an O_K-submodule L with K·L = V.
K is spherically complete for polar and bidual statements; barrelledness and Banach–Steinhaus do not need that additional assumption.
proofSteps: For a bounded closed lattice disk B in a semi-complete V, the gauge on its span is a Banach norm. In a countable LB presentation the Banach-disk factorization theorem places its image in one Banach stage of the presentation (Emerton 1.1.10–1.1.11). Hence uniform convergence on bounded sets agrees with the inverse-limit strong-operator topology (1.1.22). Banach-domain/Frechet-target operator spaces are complete by bounded-sets-strong-dual and have a countable seminorm basis, giving 1.1.23.

The Fréchet-dual polar input is the Baire factorization lemma used in the proof of Emerton 1.1.24: in a countable complete target, continuity on the strong dual of a Fréchet space produces a neighbourhood with bounded image. Treat this as an explicit part of this key target, not as a universal assertion about maps of locally convex spaces.

Apply that input to f′:F′_b→V′_b, whose target is Fréchet by the operator-space result. Since V is bornological, bounded subsets of V′_b are equicontinuous. Taking pseudo-polars, and using the bipolar theorem, produces an open lattice of V mapped into a bounded closed disk of F. Its gauge span is Banach and yields the factorization (Emerton 1.1.15 and 1.1.24).

nodes.title: Completed tensors as limits of finite-rank operators
nodes.statement: For Banach K-spaces A and B over spherically complete K, let CC(A,B) be the closure in L_b(A,B) of continuous finite-rank maps. The map A′_b ⊗ B → L_b(A,B), ℓ⊗b ↦ (a↦ℓ(a)b), is an embedding for the projective tensor topology and extends to a topological isomorphism A′_b ⊗̂_π B ≅ CC(A,B). Thus this completion represents the closure of finite-rank operators, not all continuous operators in general. The same comparison holds for arbitrary locally convex A,B whenever L_b(A,B) is complete; only its Banach specialization is required for tensor injectivity here.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·|, with ring of integers O_K = {a : |a| ≤ 1} and a fixed π ∈ K with 0 < |π| < 1; a lattice in a K-vector space V is an O_K-submodule L with K·L = V.
K is spherically complete for polar and bidual statements; barrelledness and Banach–Steinhaus do not need that additional assumption.
proofSteps: Schneider Lemma 18.1 compares tensor gauges with bounded-convergence operator seminorms. For a bounded disk D in A, pseudo-bipolarity identifies the closure of its evaluation image in the weak bidual with (D^p)^p. This gives the equality of seminorms and hence the embedding.

Finite-rank continuous operators are exactly the image of A′⊗B (choose a finite basis of the image and its continuous coordinates). Completeness of L_b(A,B) follows for Banach A,B from bounded-sets-strong-dual. Therefore the completion of the embedded tensor product is its closure, CC(A,B), as in Schneider 18.2.

nodes.statement: For injective continuous linear maps f:A₀→A₁ and g:B₀→B₁ between Banach spaces over spherically complete K, f ⊗̂_π g is injective. The original maps need not be topological embeddings. No claim is made that their tensor map is an embedding or that the hypothesis can be removed over nonspherically-complete fields.
hypotheses: K is a field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·|, with ring of integers O_K = {a : |a| ≤ 1} and a fixed π ∈ K with 0 < |π| < 1; a lattice in a K-vector space V is an O_K-submodule L with K·L = V.

gaps.title: Strict duality for extensions of spaces of compact type
gaps.detail: For a strict short exact sequence 0 → W₁ → W → W₂ → 0 over spherically complete K with compact-type outer terms, retain the unproved inputs (H1) strict exactness of 0 → W₂′_b → W′_b → W₁′_b → 0 and (H2) continuity of W → (W′_b)′_b. They suffice for compact-type-extension-duality. A sufficient criterion for H1 is that W′_b be Fréchet: the end duals are Fréchet, the annihilator is closed, and Banach/Fréchet open mapping makes both maps strict. Bounded lifting from W₂ addresses the topology of the first transpose but is not asserted equivalent to H1 or sufficient for H2. Bornological or barrelled W implies H2 by the bidual theorem. Split extensions and finite-dimensional kernel extensions are established special cases. The predecessor compact-type-three-space target must remain conditional on this gap during assembly.
